surveyDefinition.title: Running Shoes — consumer survey (India)
surveyDefinition.studyPurpose: Identify which of 4 behavioural segments each respondent belongs to, based on running frequency, purchase drivers, fit and durability priorities, and price sensitivity.

segments.name: High-Frequency Performance Runners
segments.description: Run multiple times per week, prioritize cushioning, durability, and breathability, willing to pay premium for performance technology, replace shoes every 3-6 months.

segments.name: Price-Sensitive Value Buyers
segments.description: Run occasionally or regularly but are highly price-conscious, look for durable shoes at mid-range prices, often wait for promotions, and are willing to switch brands for better value.

segments.name: Comfort-Focused Casual Runners
segments.description: Run or jog occasionally for fitness or leisure, prioritize comfort and fit over performance, prefer breathable shoes for warm climates, and are less brand-loyal.

segments.name: Style-Driven Lifestyle Buyers
segments.description: Buy running shoes for casual wear and fashion as much as for running, value design and brand image, are willing to pay for style, and may own multiple pairs.

surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A segmentation study of Running Shoes buyers in India. It asks how people use Running Shoes, how they choose it, and what would make them switch — then sorts respondents into the behavioural groups defined below. Questions stay at category level: no named brands, and nothing about adjacent categories.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in India who buy or use Running Shoes for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Individuals who have bought running shoes in the past 12 months; Individuals who run or exercise regularly (at least once a week); Individuals who are the primary decision-maker for their own shoe purchase. Excluded: Professional athletes whose shoes are provided by sponsors; Businesses purchasing shoes for employees or resale; Children under 18 (unless purchasing for themselves, but typically parent decides).
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Everyday consumers buy running shoes for personal use, pay for them out of pocket, and decide which pair to purchase based on fit, style, and performance. While some businesses may purchase shoes for employees (e.g., athletic teams), the dominant and defining buyer is the individual consumer.
respondentBehaviours: Engages in running or jogging at least occasionally
Purchases athletic footwear for fitness, sport, or casual wear
Researches brands, reviews, and features before buying
May be brand loyal or open to switching based on price/performance
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income as behavioural questions — no finding in this survey is driven by them. They are asked once, at the end, in Profiling, and used only to cross-tabulate the behavioural results.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are modelled estimates built from published market evidence — they are not measurements from fielded interviews, and should be read as an expected shape of response rather than a result. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with running and their current shoe ownership, then moves into how they shop and what drives their purchase decisions, followed by their preferences and expectations for the product itself, and closes with satisfaction, pain points, and future intentions. This arc separates the four segments by capturing frequency, price sensitivity, feature priorities, and switching behaviour.

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Running Shoes in India — who Individuals who have bought running shoes in the past 12 months; Individuals who run or exercise regularly (at least once a week); Individuals who are the primary decision-maker for their own shoe purchase. The survey targets the end consumer who buys and uses running shoes for personal fitness and lifestyle. This audience represents the primary market for running shoes globally.

metadata.studyPurpose: Identify which of 4 behavioural segments each respondent belongs to, based on running frequency, purchase drivers, fit and durability priorities, and price sensitivity.
metadata.segmentation_lens: Combination of usage/behavioural and price sensitivity, because in the APAC running shoe market, buyers genuinely differ on how often they run and how much they are willing to pay for performance and durability, while attitudes alone are weak predictors.

segments.name: High-Frequency Performance Runners
segments.description: Run multiple times per week, prioritize cushioning, durability, and breathability, willing to pay premium for performance technology, replace shoes every 3-6 months.
segments.hypothesis: They will show high spend, low price sensitivity, and strong preference for performance features over style.

segments.name: Price-Sensitive Value Buyers
segments.description: Run occasionally or regularly but are highly price-conscious, look for durable shoes at mid-range prices, often wait for promotions, and are willing to switch brands for better value.
segments.hypothesis: They will show high price sensitivity, prioritize durability and price over brand, and have longer replacement cycles.

segments.name: Comfort-Focused Casual Runners
segments.description: Run or jog occasionally for fitness or leisure, prioritize comfort and fit over performance, prefer breathable shoes for warm climates, and are less brand-loyal.
segments.hypothesis: They will show moderate frequency, high importance on comfort and breathability, and medium price sensitivity.

segments.name: Style-Driven Lifestyle Buyers
segments.description: Buy running shoes for casual wear and fashion as much as for running, value design and brand image, are willing to pay for style, and may own multiple pairs.
segments.hypothesis: They will show lower running frequency, higher importance on style and brand, and medium-to-low price sensitivity.

fieldingNotes.recommendedSample: n=800-1,200 for stable segment-level sub-groups (roughly n>=312 per segment after weighting). At n=1,000 the margin of error on a whole-sample percentage is about ±3.1pp at 95% confidence; on a segment of n=200 it widens to about ±6.9pp, so segment-level differences under ~10pp should not be reported as real.
fieldingNotes.quotaControls: Apply quotas on the category-usage and frequency screeners so heavy users — who are more willing survey-takers — are not over-sampled.
scriptingNotes: Rotate the order of answer options on every non-ordinal question to remove primacy bias. Do NOT rotate ordinal scales (frequency bands, price bands, satisfaction) — their order carries meaning.
Anchor 'Other', 'None of these' and 'Prefer not to say' to the bottom of the list, exempt from rotation.
Every 'Other' option takes an open-text capture, coded back into the frame at analysis if any single verbatim exceeds 3%.
No routing or skip logic: every respondent sees every question, so the base is constant across the instrument.
Include one attention check in the middle third — a standard instructed-response item. Terminate on failure and replace.
Randomise the order of the two ranking/trade-off items between respondents so neither is systematically answered while fresher.
caveats: Percentages in this document are modelled from published market evidence, not measured from fielded interviews. Replace them with primary data once the study is run.
Ranking items are shown as a lighter-weight ranking exercise; run them as MaxDiff if you need more precision on driver importance.
Profiling questions are for cross-tabs only and are excluded from the segmentation scoring model.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with running and their current shoe ownership, then moves into how they shop and what drives their purchase decisions, followed by their preferences and expectations for the product itself, and closes with satisfaction, pain points, and future intentions. This arc separates the four segments by capturing frequency, price sensitivity, feature priorities, and switching behaviour.
storyline_notes: Added a dedicated beat on fit and sizing in the consumer profile section, as it is a top pain point in APAC and critical for segment differentiation.
Included a beat on replacement cycle in buying behavior, which is essential for running shoes and helps identify heavy vs light users.
Added a beat on sustainability claims in preferences, reflecting the growing but still medium environmental awareness in the region.
Emphasized breathability and durability throughout, as these are top purchase drivers and pain points in the APAC climate.
Kept price-related questions late in each section to respect sensitivity, but ensured they are present to separate price-sensitive segments.
metadata.classification_reason: Everyday consumers buy running shoes for personal use, pay for them out of pocket, and decide which pair to purchase based on fit, style, and performance. While some businesses may purchase shoes for employees (e.g., athletic teams), the dominant and defining buyer is the individual consumer.
